answer: An agent marketplace requires each voting identity to lock tokens for 30 days and weights votes by the amount locked. Agents named meadow, onyx, and raven can each participate, but splitting one deposit among a thousand identities gives an attacker no extra voting power: the weights still sum to the same stake. To gain more influence, the attacker must buy and immobilize more tokens, paying both their market price and the cost of tying up capital.
